title: The life class rules
description: Windows, solvents and energy sources of the nine life classes (docs/design/habitability/life-classes.md section 3). Every number carries its source tier (T1 to T9) and tweak level (L0 to L4) next to it. A quantity the body does not store makes a rule that reads it fail (the class scores 0 and the sweep names the quantity); a supply that is not stored yet is a stated placeholder (GEN.887).
reference_basis: The Sun's effective temperature and the band of Class 1a; a class's light energy is its band's share of the star's photons over the Sun's share of 400 to 700 nm, capped at 1 (the pigment's band times the spectrum, GEN.878)

classes.name: Oxygenic light-eaters: visible pigment (Chlorophyll a)
classes.eats: light 400 to 700 nm, carbon dioxide and water, plus nitrogen, phosphorus and iron
classes.breathes: oxygen once it exists (aerobes); before that nothing
classes.gives_off: oxygen (net, after the sinks fill) and buried organic carbon; methane only through a small food web

solvent.basis: Liquid water; the index's own L_solv (water activity and chaotropicity) applies

energy.basis: A star spectrum rich in 400 to 700 nm: F, G, K and bright early M; the Sun's share of photons in the band is the reference (efficiency 1)

gates.basis: Sunlit water: an open surface ocean or a hycean sea (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 and 2 window); under ice or in an aquifer there is no light
The pigments that harvest light need air (10 Pa or more), the gate the old LIFE_CHEMICALS table used (GEN.92, GEN.647)
Carbon dioxide at least about 5 Pa for a carbon fixer (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window)
Light in the pigment's band at least 1 percent of Earth's (life-classes.md 3.1); the 0.01 percent allowance for deep microbes waits for the habitat-depth model

windows.basis: Mean habitat 255 to 395 K for microbes (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window); smooth falloff outside like the index's own terms

classes.note: Class 1a on an Earth-like world is exactly today's PHI_bio (life-classes.md 8.1). The old oxygen gate of Chlorophyll a is gone: Class 1 makes the oxygen (GEN.855).

classes.name: Anoxygenic light-eaters (Bacteriochlorophylls)
classes.eats: near-infrared light 800 to 1050 nm, carbon dioxide and a donor: hydrogen, ferrous iron or hydrogen sulfide
classes.gives_off: sulfate, sulfur, Fe(III), organic carbon; methane from their food web
classes.reaches: Microbial mats; animals only if another oxidant source exists

energy.basis: Near-infrared light, 800 to 1050 nm; the lower photon energy costs efficiency (T7)

gates.basis: Sunlit water: an open surface ocean or a hycean sea (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 and 2 window); under ice or in an aquifer there is no light
The pigments that harvest light need air (10 Pa or more), the gate the old LIFE_CHEMICALS table used (GEN.92, GEN.647)
Carbon dioxide at least about 5 Pa for a carbon fixer (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window)

Free oxygen below 3 percent poisons an anoxygenic or hydrogen-eating microbe: the existing gate (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 2 window)

supply.basis: The donor supply (hydrogen, Fe2+ or H2S delivered) is not stored yet (GEN.887); the placeholder 1 assumes an anoxic ocean has its donors

classes.name: Hydrogen eaters: geochemical hydrogen (serpentinisation, vents)
classes.eats: hydrogen from rock and water, and carbon dioxide

solvent.basis: Liquid water in contact with rock (ocean, ice-covered ocean or aquifer)

energy.basis: The share of the body's heat flow that life can use (CHEMICAL_SHARE), as the index already scores sub-ice life; no light needed

gates.basis: Any pressure: a deep ocean or aquifer is not exposed to the air

windows.basis: Mean habitat 255 to 395 K for microbes (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window); smooth falloff outside like the index's own terms

supply.basis: The hydrogen supply from serpentinisation (rock type, water, heat) is not stored yet (GEN.887); the placeholder 1 assumes ultramafic rock is present

classes.name: Hydrogen eaters: radiolytic hydrogen and sulfate (deep crust, aquifers)
classes.eats: hydrogen from the radiolysis of water, and carbon dioxide or sulfate

solvent.basis: Liquid water in contact with rock

energy.basis: The share of the body's heat flow that life can use; radiogenic heat and dose make the hydrogen

gates.basis: Any pressure: a deep ocean or aquifer is not exposed to the air

windows.basis: Mean habitat 255 to 395 K for microbes (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window); smooth falloff outside like the index's own terms

supply.basis: Radiolytic hydrogen from the rock's uranium, thorium and potassium and the water is not stored yet (GEN.887); the placeholder 1 assumes enough

classes.name: Sulfur, iron and nitrogen eaters: oxygen as the oxidant

classes.reaches: Animals (chemosymbiotic tubeworm, clam and mussel communities)

energy.basis: The energy of the fuel meeting the oxidant, scored on the share of the heat flow life can use

gates.basis: An oxygen sea: oxygen at least 0.1 percent of the air for the oxidant to reach the vents (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 4 window)

windows.basis: Mean habitat 255 to 395 K for microbes (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 1 window); smooth falloff outside like the index's own terms

supply.basis: The reduced fuel supply (H2S, Fe2+, NH4+, CH4) is not stored yet (GEN.887); the placeholder 1 assumes vents or seeps supply it

classes.name: Acid-world life: cloud-deck plankton
classes.eats: reduced sulfur, organic carbon, blue and UV light
classes.breathes: the acid itself (reduced to SO2 and sulfur); traces of oxygen
classes.reaches: Mats and aerial plankton; at most simple colonial forms

solvent.basis: Concentrated sulfuric acid as the liquid; the existing SOLVENT_FACTOR of sulfuric acid, 0.1 (planetGen's choice)

energy.basis: Chemical energy of the acid medium; light too in the cloud layer

gates.basis: A liquid sulfuric acid layer is present: nothing in the generator models it yet (GEN.888), so this class scores 0 until then

classes.name: Acid-world life: pool and crust mats

solvent.basis: Concentrated sulfuric acid as the liquid; SOLVENT_FACTOR 0.1

energy.basis: Chemical energy of the acid medium

gates.basis: A liquid sulfuric acid pool is present: not modelled yet (GEN.888)

windows.basis: Warm dry ground, acid pools 283 to 373 K (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 5b window)

classes.name: Dense-CO2 life
classes.breathes: carbon dioxide (the solvent is the oxidant)

solvent.basis: Liquid or supercritical CO2 as the solvent; no existing factor, 0.1 like the other strange solvents (planetGen's choice)

energy.basis: Chemical energy of hydrogen fuel, scored on the share of the heat flow life can use

gates.basis: A dense CO2 air or sea: carbon dioxide at least half of the air (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 6 window)
Liquid CO2 needs above 5.2 bar (the triple point is 5.18 bar)
The CO2 is liquid or supercritical at the surface

windows.basis: Liquid below 304 K, supercritical above that and about 73 bar (life-classes.md 3.1)

supply.basis: The hydrogen supply is not stored yet (GEN.887); 0.5 stands for a half of Class 3's

solvent.basis: The existing SOLVENT_FACTOR of a hydrocarbon sea, 0.2 (planetGen's choice); the index's `solvent()` rule says when a methane sea exists

energy.basis: Chemical energy of hydrogen and acetylene, scored on the share of the heat flow life can use

windows.basis: N2 and CH4 air around 1.5 bar (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 7 window)

supply.basis: The hydrogen and acetylene supply (haze organics) is not stored yet (GEN.887); 0.5 is a stand-in

classes.name: Ammonia-water life
classes.eats: hydrogen and chemical gradients in cold alkaline brine

solvent.basis: Water with ammonia as the liquid; 0.1 like the other strange solvents (planetGen's choice)

energy.basis: Chemical energy of hydrogen and gradients, scored on the share of the heat flow life can use

gates.basis: Ammonia at least 10 percent of the water mass (life-classes.md 3.1, Class 8 window); the ammonia inventory is not stored yet (GEN.887), so this class scores 0 until then

windows.basis: 176 to 273 K: the water-ammonia eutectic is about 176 K (recalled)

supply.basis: The hydrogen supply is not stored yet (GEN.887); 0.5 is a stand-in

solvent.basis: Concentrated sulfuric acid as the liquid; SOLVENT_FACTOR 0.1

energy.basis: Chemical energy of the acid medium

gates.basis: A liquid sulfuric acid layer or pool is present: not modelled yet (GEN.888)
A silicon-rich crust (GEN.441 crust composition); not exposed as a quantity yet

windows.basis: As Class 5; silicones resist 98 percent acid at 90 C (life-classes.md 3.1, read in the climates report)

non_water_chemistry.basis: The index's chemistry term needs carbon, nitrogen and hydrogen in Earth units, and hydrogen comes from the water; a class that does not drink water gets its hydrogen from the supply term (GEN.887), so its inventory is held at this floor, and phosphate is the index's NON_AQUEOUS_PHOSPHATE_UMOL_L
